html:
Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk was a philosopher and politician, born in 1850 in Hodonín in Moravia to a Slovak father and a Moravian mother, who founded Czechoslovakia and was its first president from 1918 to 1935.

As a professor in Prague he exposed forged medieval manuscripts that nationalists cherished, and he defended a Jewish man wrongly accused of ritual murder. In World War I he went abroad and with Edvard Beneš and Milan Štefánik won Allied support for a Czech and Slovak state, helped by the Czechoslovak Legion fighting in Russia. Czechoslovakia was proclaimed on 28 October 1918. He kept it a democracy when most of its neighbours became dictatorships. Garrigue was his American wife's surname. He died in 1937, a year before the Munich Agreement.
sum: Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk was a philosopher and politician, born in 1850 in Hodonín in Moravia to a Slovak father and a Moravian mother, who founded Czechoslovakia and was its first president from 1918 to 1935.
